summary: This TRL evidence pack, dated 12 November 2026, documents new evidence for a centriole-tracking readout system used to study cell division dynamics. It presents results from a synthetic benchmark simulation (phantom_bench.py), quantifies detection performance under multiple degradation conditions, reports a software test count of 29 total tests, and outlines four planned milestones that would advance the platform from TRL 3 toward TRL 4 without requiring wet-lab biology results.

content_blocks.title: Document Purpose and Deposit
content_blocks.content: The document is a TRL evidence pack dated 12 November 2026. The benchmark is published with DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24148459 (CC-BY-4.0), including the script, frozen seed, and checksum. Purpose: to list evidence as of 12 November 2026, state what each item does and does not prove, and give the software test count with two reproducible commands.

content_blocks.title: Section 1: Synthetic Benchmark — Overview and Protocol
content_blocks.content: A synthetic benchmark was run to measure the centriole-detection and lineage-tracking chain against ground truth for the first time. The protocol chain is: detect centrioles → keep identity across divisions → compute old-vs-new division-rate dynamics. Run on 12 November 2026 using script phantom/phantom_bench.py (seed 20261112), 96 frames at 30-minute cadence, 40 simulated cells, four degradation conditions plus a threshold-control pair. Metrics file checksum stored as out/metrics.json.sha256 for reproducibility.

content_blocks.title: Synthetic Benchmark Results by Degradation Condition
content_blocks.content:
Five conditions tested with position RMSE, detection recall, and detection precision:

1. Resolvable sampling (pairs 6–9 px apart, ≈80 nm/px): RMSE=0.38 px, Recall=0.78, Precision=0.92
2. Under-resolved (pairs 2–3 px apart, ≈250 nm/px): RMSE=1.25 px, Recall=0.46, Precision=0.99
3. Low signal-to-noise (⅓ of nominal photons): RMSE=0.41 px, Recall=0.79, Precision=0.89
4. Defocus (1.9 px blur instead of 1.1): RMSE=0.34 px, Recall=0.30, Precision=0.52
5. High drift (4× drift rate, 8 px amplitude): RMSE=0.38 px, Recall=0.78, Precision=0.92

content_blocks.title: Key Findings from Synthetic Benchmark
content_blocks.content:
Three results highlighted as most important:
1. Hard sampling requirement quantified: ≤100 nm/px at the sample, no binning above 2×2. Below this, recall=0.78 with near-zero false positives. Above (250 nm/px), recall halves and centriole pairs merge — producing plausible but wrong lineage data. This is now a candidate functional requirement not previously in the requirements document.
2. Defocus costs recall before accuracy (recall=0.30, precision=0.52 at 1.9 px blur) — measured justification for treating focus hold as the P0 engineering item, consistent with engineering audit of Zeiss Axio Observer 7.
3. Power calculation: ~115 cells per group needed to detect a 2-hour difference in interdivision interval at α=0.05, power=0.8, given measured localisation error and 6-hour between-cell spread. A dozen cells cannot decide this question.

content_blocks.title: Limitations of Synthetic Benchmark
content_blocks.content: Explicitly stated limitations: (1) It is a simulation, not real data. (2) Says nothing about whether inherited centriole age predicts division timing — untested biology outside this phase's claims. (3) Cell model is crude (Gaussian body, two Gaussian centrioles, rigid motion). (4) PSF is Gaussian rather than physical. (5) Tracker is a reference implementation with constant-velocity prediction, not the production lineage tracker. (6) Division timing is counted in the phantom but not yet scored as an endpoint.

content_blocks.title: TRL Positioning Statement
content_blocks.content: For the analysis chain, the synthetic benchmark constitutes the experimental proof of concept that TRL 3 requires: a specified function demonstrated in a controlled setting with quantitative error. For the biology, nothing moves — TRL for the biological hypothesis is unchanged.

content_blocks.title: Section 2: Software Test Count
content_blocks.content:
Two reproducible commands produce the test count:
- pytest tests in software/: 12 passed
- #[test] functions in software/argus-agent: 17
- Total in working tree: 29
This count is carried in supplement v1.1 and the ninety-day plan. The defensible form of any test claim is the verified count plus the command, commit, and CI run.

content_blocks.title: Section 3: Planned Evidence and What It Would Establish
content_blocks.content:
Four planned items that would advance readiness:
1. Focus-hold prototype with 72h drift log → closes P0 hardware gap; supports instrument TRL 4 | Status: plan, due 15 Jan 2027
2. Unattended run on fixed samples producing machine-readable tracked-division log → instrument and software validated in lab on real optics | Status: plan, due 31 Jan 2027
3. Protocol pre-registered with sampling requirement and power calculation → removes 'analysis can drift' objection | Status: ready to deposit, after this note
4. Division-timing error scored in the phantom → closes endpoint the benchmark deliberately left open | Status: next iteration

Note: None of these four requires a wet-lab biology result. All are producible by one person with hardware in hand.

content_blocks.title: Section 4: Reproduce — Commands
content_blocks.content:
Exact commands to reproduce all results:
- cd phantom && python3 phantom_bench.py  # ~6 minutes, one core
- python3 make_report.py  # regenerates report from metrics.json
- sha256sum out/metrics.json  # compare against out/metrics.json.sha256
- cd ../.. && (cd software && python3 -m pytest -q tests)  # 12 passed
- grep -rn "#[test]" software/argus-agent/src | wc -l  # 17

key_findings: Synthetic benchmark (phantom_bench.py, seed 20261112, 12 Nov 2026) is the first quantitative ground-truth measurement of the centriole-detection and lineage-tracking chain, deposited with DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24148459.

Hard sampling requirement quantified: ≤100 nm/px at sample, no binning above 2×2. At 250 nm/px (under-resolved), recall drops from 0.78 to 0.46 and centriole pairs merge, producing wrong lineage data.
Defocus is the dominant failure mode: at 1.9 px blur, recall=0.30 and precision=0.52, providing measured justification for focus hold as the P0 engineering priority (Zeiss Axio Observer 7 context).
Power calculation: ~115 cells per group required to detect a 2-hour difference in interdivision interval at α=0.05, power=0.8 — a requirement not previously in the protocol.
For the analysis chain, the benchmark constitutes TRL 3 proof of concept (specified function demonstrated in controlled setting with quantitative error). Biology TRL is unchanged.
Software test count: 29 total (12 pytest in software/, 17 #[test] in argus-agent), reproducible via two stated commands.

Four planned milestones (focus-hold prototype, unattended run on fixed samples, protocol pre-registration, division-timing scoring in phantom) would advance platform toward TRL 4 without wet-lab biology.
Limitations: simulation only, crude cell model (Gaussian), Gaussian PSF (not physical), reference tracker (not production), division timing not yet scored as endpoint.
